title: Compact-support site comparison respects compactification calculus
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$, $n\geq1$. All schemes below are finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], without a separatedness assumption on their structure maps to $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Every morphism $f:X\to Y$ to which compact support is applied is separated and finite type and has a chosen compactification $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X,p:\overline X\to Y)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], comparison $C_T=\nu_T^*$ [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], and compact-support candidates $F_f^{e,c}=Rp_{e,*}j_!^e$, $F_f^{p,c}=Rp_{p,*}j_!^p$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support, def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. Define
$$B_f^c=Rp_{p,*}(e_j)\circ\beta_{p,j_!^e}:C_YF_f^{e,c}\longrightarrow F_f^{p,c}C_X,$$
where $\beta_p$ is the counit-mate direct-image comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] and $e_j:C_{\overline X}j_!^e\cong j_!^pC_X$ is the adjoint extension-by-zero comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]. On $D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, $B_f^c$ is invertible and has the following coherence with the canonical compactification maps. For composable separated finite-type morphisms $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to Z$ with chosen compactifications and compatible composition towers, and for two compactifications $c,c'$ of $f$ with a specified proper refinement, use the refinement comparisons $\rho^{e}_{c',c}:F_f^{e,c}\to F_f^{e,c'}$ and $\rho^p_{c',c}:F_f^{p,c}\to F_f^{p,c'}$, and composition comparisons $\alpha^e_{g,f}:F_g^eF_f^e\to F_{gf}^e$, $\alpha^p_{g,f}:F_g^pF_f^p\to F_{gf}^p$ of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons, thm-sf-comp-composition],
$$B_f^{c'}C_Y(\rho^e_{c',c})=\rho^p_{c',c}C_X\circ B_f^c,$$
$$B_{gf}C_Z(\alpha^e_{g,f})=\alpha^p_{g,f}C_X\circ(F_g^pB_f)\circ(B_gF_f^e).$$
For an open immersion $v:Y'\hookrightarrow Y$ and its Cartesian pullback $u:X'\hookrightarrow X$, let $f':X'\to Y'$ be the pullback and use the pulled-back compactification. The canonical compact-support restriction exchanges $\operatorname{Ex}^e:v_e^*F_f^e\to F_{f'}^eu_e^*$ and $\operatorname{Ex}^p:v_p^*F_f^p\to F_{f'}^pu_p^*$ are invertible and obey
$$\operatorname{Ex}^p\circ v_p^*B_f=B_{f'}u_e^*\circ C_{Y'}(\operatorname{Ex}^e),$$
under the canonical pullback comparisons. All these identities use the normalized proper/open interchanges in compatible compactification towers, including commutative proper/open squares which are not Cartesian, and the counit-mate normalization above; they hold on bounded-below etale witnesses. They respect identities and pasting.

proof.text: All ambient schemes in the chosen compactifications and compatible towers are finite type over the field: their proper maps are finite type, and their targets are finite type. Since a field is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes these schemes Noetherian. Every open subscheme of a Noetherian scheme is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Applied also to the inverse images of affine opens, this verifies that the open immersions are quasi-compact. Thus the open maps in the towers satisfy the quasi-compact hypothesis below, and proper maps are qcqs. The definitions of the compact-support candidates give the bounded-below composites used here. Exactness and bounded-below preservation of \(C_T\) follow from [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]; the canonical comparisons \(C_Uu_e^*\cong u_p^*C_V\) respect identities, composites and squares by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. In the remaining equations these pullback comparisons and the canonical functor associators are inserted implicitly.

source.place: Tag 099R, section-comparison; Noetherian and bounded-below hypotheses for the stated DAG tools

proof.text:
For \(c=(j,p)\), the named map \(\beta_p:C_YRp_{e,*}\to Rp_{p,*}C_{\overline X}\) is invertible on bounded-below etale inputs by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. Its normalization is
\[\varepsilon^p_p\,p_p^*(\beta_p)\,a_p=C_{\overline X}(\varepsilon^e_p),\]
where \(a_p:C_{\overline X}p_e^*\cong p_p^*C_Y\). The canonical adjoint open comparison \(e_j:C_{\overline X}j_!^e\cong j_!^pC_X\) is the isomorphism of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], applied termwise. Consequently \(B_f^c=Rp_{p,*}(e_j)\,\beta_{p,j_!^e}\) is an isomorphism with exactly the specified normalization. Moreover, the direct-image comparisons compose by the composite-adjunction formula in [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], since their pullback comparisons compose. The open comparisons compose by the open-composition clause of the cited extension comparison.

proof.text:
Fix a commutative proper/open square \(Q\) with top \(k:V\hookrightarrow W\), bottom \(i:S\hookrightarrow T\), and proper sides \(r:V\to S\), \(p:W\to T\). Write \(\gamma_Q^s:i_!^sRr_{s,*}\to Rp_{s,*}k_!^s\), \(s=e,p\), for its normalized comparison. Apply [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus] with \(B=A\), every finite ring \(\Lambda_m=A\), every scalar map the identity, and the constant strict tower on \(C_VL\), for \(L\in D^+(V_{\mathrm{et}},A)\). Its finite-evaluation clause identifies the evaluated named pro-etale arrow, under the canonical direct-image and open comparisons, with \(\gamma_Q^e\) of [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence]. The scalar transport is the identity specialization of [def-cbc-finite-constant-coefficient-transport]. Writing those source and target identifications explicitly gives
\[\gamma_Q^p\,(i_!^p\beta_r)\,(e_iRr_{e,*})
=(Rp_{p,*}e_k)\,(\beta_pk_!^e)\,C_T(\gamma_Q^e).\tag{N}\]
Both sides go from \(C_Ti_!^eRr_{e,*}L\) to \(Rp_{p,*}k_!^pC_VL\). This is a specialization of the stated finite-evaluation normalization, not an inference from faithfulness of tower evaluation. It includes non-Cartesian squares and the clopen-section refinement normalization. The tower lemma also supplies actual pro-etale horizontal, vertical and base-change pasting; its etale counterpart is [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence].

source.place: Tags 0F7B, 0F7C, 0F7D, 0F7F for etale maps; the cited strict-tower node supplies the additional pro-etale finite-evaluation normalization (agent specialization)

proof.text:
Let \(u:c_1\to c_2\), so \(uj_1=j_2\) and \(p_1=p_2u\); put \(c=c_1,c'=c_2\). The proper/open arrow is
\(a_u^s:j_{2!}^s\to Ru_{s,*}j_{1!}^s\), directed opposite to the refinement comparison after proper pushforward. Precisely, if \(\kappa^s:R(p_2u)_{s,*}\cong Rp_{2,s,*}Ru_{s,*}\), then
\[\rho^s_{c_2,c_1}=Rp_{2,s,*}((a_u^s)^{-1})\,\kappa^s.\]
This is the formula in [def-sf-refinement-comparison-isomorphism] on the pro-etale identity witness, and the proper-refinement comparison of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] on the etale side. The specialization of (N) to \(V=S=X,r=1,p=u,k=j_1,i=j_2\) is exactly [lem-sf-proper-open-comparison-site-normalization]:
\[a_u^p e_{j_2}=(Ru_{p,*}e_{j_1})\,\beta_u\,C(a_u^e).\]
Multiplying by the inverses of \(a_u^p\) and \(C(a_u^e)\) gives
\[e_{j_2}C((a_u^e)^{-1})=(a_u^p)^{-1}(Ru_{p,*}e_{j_1})\beta_u.\]
Apply \(Rp_{2,p,*}\), use naturality of \(\beta_{p_2}\), and use its composition formula from Step 2 to replace the comparisons for \(p_2,u\) by that for \(p_1\). The left side becomes \(B_f^{c_2}C_Y(\rho^e_{c_2,c_1})\), and the right side becomes \((\rho^p_{c_2,c_1}C_X)B_f^{c_1}\). This proves the refinement identity without reversing either named arrow.

source.place: Tags 0F7B and 0F7C; main-20261015 blueprint prop-compactification-coherence proof, inverse proper/open formula; agent inverse-and-pushforward calculation

proof.text:
Choose a compatible tower from [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower]: \(Y\xrightarrow{i}\overline Y\xrightarrow{q}Z\), \(X\xrightarrow{a}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}\overline Y\), and \(U=\overline X\times_{\overline Y}Y\), with \(b:U\hookrightarrow\overline X\), \(r:U\to Y\) proper and \(c:X\hookrightarrow U\), so \(bc=a\). For the Cartesian square \(Q=(b,i;r,p)\), the normalized tower convention in the item defines the chosen-model composition map on either site as
\[Rq_{s,*}i_!^sRr_{s,*}c_!^s
 \xrightarrow{Rq_{s,*}(\gamma_Q^s)c_!^s}
 Rq_{s,*}Rp_{s,*}b_!^sc_!^s
 \xrightarrow{\chi^s}R(qp)_{s,*}a_!^s,\]
where \(\chi^s\) is the proper-composition and open-composition identification. This is the normalized compactification-tower construction of \(\alpha^s_{g,f}\); its canonical choice-independent maps are [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons, thm-sf-comp-composition]. Apply (N) to \(L=c_!^eK\), then apply \(Rq_{p,*}\). Precompose with the comparisons for \(q\) and \(c\). Naturality of \(\beta_q\) moves it through \(\gamma_Q^e\); Step 2 identifies the proper factors with \(\beta_{qp}\) and the open factors with \(e_a\). Thus the two boundary composites of this explicit diagram are
\[B_{gf}C_Z(\alpha^e_{g,f})
=\alpha^p_{g,f}C_X\,(F_g^pB_f)\,(B_gF_f^e).\]
The input \(c_!^eK\) is bounded below, and its proper pushforward \(Rr_{e,*}c_!^eK\) is bounded below, so every application of (N) or \(\beta\) is in its stated domain.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, lemma-shriek-composition; main-20261015 thm-sf-comp-composition proof, construction; agent application of (N)

proof.text: Two compatible towers admit a common refining tower by [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower]. On its comparison to either tower the intermediate proper/open squares may be non-Cartesian. Equation (N) applies to each of these squares as well. The horizontal and vertical laws of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus] identify their pasted pro-etale comparisons with the comparison of the rectangle; [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence] does the same on the etale side. Substitute the refinement identity of Step 4 into these diagrams. The equations for the common tower and either chosen tower then have the same boundaries after conjugating by the invertible refinement maps. Hence Step 5 proves the displayed composition identity for the specified compactifications and is independent of the compatible tower. This uses the actual non-Cartesian normalization, not an etale theorem applied to a pro-etale functor.

source.place: Tags 0F7C, 0F7D and 0F7J; agent common-refinement calculation using the stated pro-etale pasting laws

proof.text:
For the open pullback \(v:Y'\hookrightarrow Y\), write \(\bar v:\overline X'\to\overline X\), \(p':\overline X'\to Y'\) for the pulled-back compactification of [def-cbc-compact-support-square]. Denote the specified proper mate exchanges by \(E^s:v_s^*Rp_{s,*}\to Rp'_{s,*}\bar v_s^*\). Their etale normalization is the module-mate formula in [def-cbc-exchange-map, lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients]; the pro-etale one is the same unit-square-counit formula, as for \(E_p^{\mathcal T}\) in [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coefficient-exchange-mates] to the four adjunctions for \(p,p'\) on the two sites. Its push-comparison hypotheses are precisely the counit equations for \(\beta_p,\beta_{p'}\) in Step 2. Its pull-comparison cube is the Cartesian compatibility of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. Therefore its conclusion gives, with those pullback identifications,
\[E^p C_{\overline X}\,v_p^*(\beta_p)
=(\beta_{p'}\bar v_e^*)\,C_{Y'}(E^e).\tag{P}\]
In particular (P) concerns the named exchanges: their transposes are \(\bar v_s^*\varepsilon_p^s\circ\theta^s\), and the counit equations turn both routes into the same transpose. No choice of an unspecified exchange isomorphism enters.

source.place: Tag 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints; explicit exchange mate of def-cbc-exchange-map; agent coefficient-cube specialization

proof.text:
Let \(h^s:\bar v_s^*j_!^s\cong j'_!{}^su_s^*\) be the canonical extension-by-zero base-change map. On the etale side it is [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change]; on the pro-etale side it is [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change]. Its precise normalization is the inverse of the open-adjunction transpose of the unit: [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change] gives this on the etale side, and [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus] gives it on the pro-etale side after the constant finite specialization of Step 3. The comparison \(e_j\) is likewise the specified adjoint comparison. Take inverses and transpose under the open adjunctions. The two possible composites of these units are equal because the pullback square commutes with site comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]; mate pasting [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] then gives
\[h^pC_X\,\bar v_p^*(e_j)
=(e_{j'}u_e^*)\,C_{\overline X'}(h^e).\tag{O}\]
More explicitly, after restriction to \(X'\), both inverse transposes send \(C_{X'}u_e^*K\) by the open unit into \(j'^*\bar v_p^*C_{\overline X}j_!^eK\); inserting the comparison of pullbacks makes both maps \(C_{X'}u_e^*(\eta^e_{j,K})\). Thus (O) identifies the specified open factors, not just their sources and targets.

source.place: Tag 09AF, lemma-jshriek-comparison; the inverse-open-mate normalizations in the cited base-change statements; agent unit calculation

proof.text:
The specified compact-support exchange on either site is
\[\operatorname{Ex}^s=(Rp'_{s,*}h^s)\,E^s_{j_!^s},\]
as in [def-cbc-exchange-map]. Expand the left side of the desired site-comparison equation using this formula and \(B_f=Rp_{p,*}(e_j)\beta_p\). Naturality of \(E^p\) moves \(e_j\) past the proper exchange. Equation (P) replaces the remaining \(E^p v_p^*\beta_p\) by \(\beta_{p'}C(E^e)\); equation (O) replaces the open factor by \(e_{j'}C(h^e)\). Naturality of \(\beta_{p'}\) then leaves exactly
\[\operatorname{Ex}^p\,v_p^*B_f
=B_{f'}u_e^*\,C_{Y'}(\operatorname{Ex}^e).\]
The etale exchange is invertible by [thm-cbc-finite-torsion], whose quasi-compact-open hypothesis was checked in Step 1. Since \(B_f,B_{f'}\) and the pullback comparisons are invertible, this same equality proves invertibility of this named \(\operatorname{Ex}^p\) on the etale witnesses. For a witness isomorphism \(C_XK\cong M\), naturality conjugates the formula by that isomorphism. No claim about arbitrary pro-etale inputs is needed.

source.place: Tag 0F7F, lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-base-change; agent expansion of the two specified factors

proof.text:
Here is also an explicit verification of identity and pasting. For each generator (refinement, composition, open restriction), Steps 4, 5 and 9 give a square \(t^p B_0=B_1C(t^e)\), where \(B_0,B_1\) include the appropriate whiskered comparisons. For two composable generators, substitution gives
\[t_2^pt_1^pB_0=t_2^pB_1C(t_1^e)
=B_2C(t_2^e)C(t_1^e)=B_2C(t_2^et_1^e).\]
The same substitution with functors whiskered proves horizontal pasting, using naturality of \(B\). Repeating it handles a finite pasted diagram. The corresponding etale identities, refinement transitivity and composition associativity are [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]; identity and horizontal/vertical exchange pasting are explicitly in [thm-cbc-finite-torsion]. Mixed proper/open rectangles satisfy the base-change equation of [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence] and its pro-etale version in [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. Thus either route through each pasted diagram becomes \(B_{\rm out}C(t^e)\) after precomposition with the same invertible \(B_{\rm in}\). Cancel it to obtain the required pro-etale equality. For an identity diagram this reads \(t^pB=B\), hence \(t^p=1\). This proves pasting on witnesses directly from the equations for the named maps.
